assumptions: Assumes transparency and notice mechanisms are tied to this grant/share action in the backend.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness here is grounded in insufficient transparency around the backend’s grant-and-share action; applicability depends on whether notice is modeled elsewhere.

title: Live-location updates enable identification and inference of the child's habits and sensitive patterns
description: Real-time location disclosures can reveal identity-linked movement patterns such as home, school, routines, religious visits, or medical appointments. Even when the recipient is an intended guardian, the flow increases the risk that the child can be profiled or that sensitive attributes can be inferred from the shared data.
assumptions: Assumes location data is granular and frequent enough to reveal patterns.
uncertainty_note: This is an inference/identifiability risk inherent to live location sharing rather than evidence of misuse by EE3.

title: Backend-mediated sharing links the child’s identity to the secondary guardian relationship and location stream
description: By granting EE3 access, the backend creates or exposes a link between the child, the secondary guardian, and the ongoing live-location feed. This relationship linkability can reveal social/family connections and facilitate correlation of future events or records involving the child and guardian.
assumptions: Assumes EE3 is associated with an identifiable account or profile and the grant is persisted or observable.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort; linkability is clearly relevant but the exact sub-node may differ across threat-tree editions.

title: Shared analytics may be linkable to partner-held datasets
description: Even if the backend shares only aggregated usage and engagement analytics, the combination of segmentation dimensions, campaign metadata, timestamps, app version, region, or cohort identifiers can let the advertising/analytics partner correlate successive disclosures or link them with other datasets it already holds, enabling linkage of user groups or potentially individuals in small cohorts.
assumptions: Assumes the shared analytics include repeated reports or dimensions granular enough for correlation, and that the partner has other data sources to combine with these analytics.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement for linkability via data sharing; exact node labeling may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Partner may infer identity from ostensibly aggregated analytics
description: The receiving partner may be able to identify individuals or very small groups from aggregate analytics when reports are broken down by narrow cohorts, locations, device characteristics, or event timing, especially when combined with external identifiers or auxiliary data already available to the partner.
assumptions: Assumes aggregation thresholds or k-anonymity protections are weak or absent and that the partner can combine the data with auxiliary datasets.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node id is best-effort; the identification risk clearly applies at the destination even if the node numbering differs.

title: Partner can learn sensitive behavior patterns from engagement analytics
description: Usage and engagement analytics can disclose sensitive traits or interests at cohort level, such as health, religion, sexuality, children-related activity, or other special-category inferences, if app features or content categories are reflected in the shared metrics. The partner may derive such sensitive information from received analytics even without direct identifiers.
assumptions: Assumes the app's engagement metrics are meaningfully associated with sensitive topics or vulnerable populations.
uncertainty_note: Node id is selected by best judgement for disclosure of sensitive information through analytics.

title: Secondary advertising use may be unexpected by users
description: Users may reasonably expect app telemetry to support service improvement, but not expect their backend-generated usage and engagement analytics to be shared with an external advertising/analytics partner to fund the free tier. This creates an unawareness risk regarding recipients, purposes, and downstream uses of the data.
assumptions: Assumes the sharing purpose and recipient are not made sufficiently clear in the app UI or privacy notice at the time of collection and use.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness strongly applies here; specific tree-node numbering may vary by catalog version.

title: Analytics sharing for ad funding may exceed consent or stated purpose
description: Sharing backend analytics with an advertising/analytics partner to monetize the free tier may be incompatible with the original collection purpose or legal basis if users did not freely consent to third-party advertising analytics, if opt-out signals are ignored, or if the data is repurposed beyond what was declared.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy requirements demand consent, purpose limitation, honoring objections/opt-outs, or contractual restrictions on onward use.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on jurisdiction, notices, and consent design; exact node id is best-effort.

title: Backend can identify the child from SOS/check-in submissions
description: The incoming check-in/SOS message contains current location and is sent from the child's account/app context to the backend. If the backend stores or processes persistent identifiers together with these events, the child becomes directly identifiable to the service operator through a highly sensitive event stream.
assumptions: Assumes the backend receives an account identifier, device token, authenticated session, or other persistent handle along with the message.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgement based on common LINDDUN identifiability structure; exact node numbering may vary by version.

title: Backend can link repeated SOS/check-in events to the same child over time
description: Manual check-ins and SOS messages with location create a longitudinal pattern. If the backend associates multiple submissions with the same child/account/device, it can link events across time and infer routines, frequent places, and emergency history.
assumptions: Assumes repeated messages are stored under a stable child, family, or device identifier.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree node numbering is approximate; applicability is high.

title: SOS/check-in content reveals the child's precise location and emergency context to the backend
description: This flow exposes personal data, specifically real-time location and the fact that the child initiated a manual check-in or SOS. These data reveal where the child is and may reveal distress, vulnerability, or safety incidents to the backend operator or anyone with backend access.
assumptions: Assumes the backend can access plaintext location and message type before any minimization or aggregation.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ between LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: The backend can detect the child's presence, movement, or emergency events from incoming messages
description: Because the child actively sends location-bearing check-in/SOS events, the backend can detect when the child is active, where they are, and when an unusual or urgent event occurs. Even sparse events can disclose presence at sensitive places or times.
assumptions: Assumes the backend observes message timestamps and locations and can distinguish SOS from routine check-ins.
uncertainty_note: Tree node numbering is best-judgement; threat applicability is strong.

title: Collection of precise child location in SOS/check-ins may exceed necessity or valid consent expectations
description: This flow involves collection of precise geolocation and emergency-context data from a child, a special-risk data subject. If the backend collects, stores, or reuses more detail than needed to notify the parent or lacks appropriate parental authorization, child-specific transparency, retention limits, or lawful basis, the flow creates non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes applicable child-privacy, location-privacy, or platform-consent obligations apply and that governance controls may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends heavily on jurisdiction, product design, and consent model; included as a conditional but credible threat.
